note: Birnbaum et al. explicitly reported short stature as an observed prevalent phenotype in their Ashkenazi Jewish cohort, contradicting the premise that it is absent.

evidence.text: Birnbaum et al. identified short stature as one of the prevalent clinical features in their Ashkenazi Jewish cohort with SGSM3-associated intellectual disability syndrome.

source.title: Intellectual disability syndrome associated with a homozygous founder variant in SGSM3 in Ashkenazi Jews

evidence.text: Turkyilmaz et al. reported two siblings with homozygous stop-gain SGSM3 variants presenting with short stature and intellectual disability.

source.title: A Strong Candidate Gene for Nonsyndromic Intellectual Disability Phenotype: SGSM3
source.quote: In this study, a novel homozygous stop-gain (NM_015705.6: c.1576C>T: p.(Arg526Ter)) variation was detected in the SGSM3 gene in two siblings with short stature and ID findings.
